_readme: Ported from the Python version. Only heap_scan mode is supported here (the other buffer.mode variants -- dotnet_string_list, ring_fixed_stride, scrolling_blob -- were legacy/unused stubs for other games, not ported). Regex patterns use .NET named-group syntax (?<name>...) instead of Python's (?P<name>...) -- same meaning, different prefix. Pattern ORDER matters: the first match wins, so the specific 'X's <ability> hits' shapes must come before the bare-verb melee shapes. Line shapes below were reconstructed/verified against real captured combat text in logs/combat_events.jsonl.
_chat_anchors_note: buffer.chat_anchors feed the Chat window (App toolbar 'Chat'). Scanned in the same heap sweep as buffer.anchors. A line found ONLY via a chat anchor -- no combat anchor, no combat-pattern match -- is shown in the Chat window and NOT run through the combat parser or the unmatched-line log. '<color=#' catches the colour-wrapped copy the game keeps of nearly every chat line. Set to [] to disable the feature.

line_patterns.name: your_pet_hit_school
line_patterns._comment: 'Your pet Rebel hits <target> for N points of <school> Damage.' -- the pet is the SOURCE (captured), so its damage lands on its own combatant row, not merged into You. MUST precede you_hit_named_ability or that pattern eats it as ability='pet Rebel', source='You'.
line_patterns.regex: ^(?:<color=#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}>)?Your pet (?<source>.+?) hits (?<target>.+?) for (?<amount>\d+) points? of (?<school>\w+) Damage\.(?:</color>)?$

line_patterns.name: your_pet_hit
line_patterns.regex: ^(?:<color=#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}>)?Your pet (?<source>.+?) hits (?<target>.+?) for (?<amount>\d+) points? of damage[.!](?:</color>)?$

line_patterns.name: other_hit_your_pet
line_patterns._comment: '<mob> bites/hits your pet Rebel for N points of damage.' -- keeps the mob as the source and the pet name as the target (was being mis-split by general_melee_hit into source='a young crypt scarab bites your'). MUST precede general_melee_hit.
line_patterns.regex: ^(?:<color=#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}>)?(?<source>.+?) (?<ability>[a-z]+) your pet (?<target>.+?) for (?<amount>\d+) points? of damage[.!](?:</color>)?$

line_patterns.name: enemy_miss_your_pet
line_patterns.regex: ^(?:<color=#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}>)?(?<source>.+?) tries to (?<ability>[a-z]+) your pet (?<target>.+?), but misses!(?:</color>)?$

line_patterns.name: you_hit_named_ability
line_patterns._comment: DoT ticks and other emphatic hits end in '!' not '.', so accept both.

line_patterns.name: general_melee_hit
line_patterns._comment: <source> <verb> <target> for N points of damage. -- covers you->mob, mob->you, and (the shape that was being dropped) other-player->mob and mob->other-player. The verb is lowercase (?<ability>[a-z]+); the target must look like a name so source/verb/target don't mis-split when the source itself has spaces ('a desert bat'). MUST stay after the named-ability patterns above.

line_patterns.name: you_engage
line_patterns._comment: Real log line is bare 'Starting to attack.' with NO target (sometimes color-wrapped). Target group is optional so both 'Starting to attack.' and a future 'Starting to attack <x>.' parse.

line_patterns.name: you_disengage
line_patterns._comment: Real log line is bare 'Stopped attacking.' with NO target (sometimes color-wrapped, incl. <color=#FF0000>).

line_patterns.name: _unconfirmed_you_resist
line_patterns._comment: GUESSED wording -- M&M spell-resist lines have never been captured. Best guess by symmetry with the game's present-tense third-person style ('a rat bites YOU'). If real resists don't announce, check logs/unmatched_<char>.log for the actual text and fix this one line.

line_patterns.name: you_slay_target
line_patterns._comment: Usually 'You have slain <target>.' but a bare 'You have slain' (no target) has been seen -- target group optional so both fire a kill.

line_patterns.name: world_time_clock
line_patterns._comment: The /time command's clock line. Confirmed wording: 'Game Time: 3 AM' (hour only; minutes assumed :00 -- the ':MM' group is there in case some times show them). Leading '.*?' tolerates a channel/timestamp prefix if chat adds one. MeterState packs the game minute-of-day into the event's Amount and feeds it to the GameClock (a full M&M day = 72 real minutes).

line_patterns.name: world_date
line_patterns._comment: The /time command's calendar line: 'The date is Tilusten, the 4th of Harvesttide in the year 608 After the Reformation. It is Autumn'. Held verbatim for display; event Amount is -1 to mark it as a date (not a clock) update.
